content.text:
I pulled all three surfaces and diffed them. Here's what I found, then my answers to your feedback, then questions.

## Answers to your feedback

**1. Remove the legacy references (SKILL.md:32-33) — agree on one, disagree on the other.**

The PNG should go. It's 2.8 MB, it's a screenshot, and nothing can be verified against it.

But `references/liatrio-brand-guidelines.md` is mislabeled, not stale. I extracted the icon inventory from the live brand page's JS chunk and diffed it against that file: 120 icons on the site, 120 in the file, zero difference in either direction. Its color tables match `brand-data.json` exactly. Its Components and Spacing sections are the only record anywhere of the live brand site's component inventory — `brand-data.json` has no components or icons section at all, and neither does the zip. Only three things in it are genuinely stale: the DM Sans typography section, the `liatrio.com` URLs, and the "Legacy" framing itself.

So deleting it would throw away the only current record of the canonical icon set. My recommendation is to strip the stale parts, repoint URLs to `liatrio.ai`, rename it to something like `references/liatrio-brand-site.md`, and treat it as a current sibling source rather than a legacy tier.

**2. Implementation Decision Format — agree, delete it.**

The Brand Audit contract is a real deliverable; an audit *is* a document. "Implementation Decision" is a report *about* work rather than the work itself, so it pushes the agent to narrate instead of build. The adherence checker enforces the Brand Audit fields and enforces nothing here. And its five bullets restate the Workflow Checklist and Verification Loop. If you want the traceability, one line in the verification loop asking the agent to state the tokens and asset paths it used covers it.

**3. The two shell scripts — agree, delete both.**

Beyond the Windows portability point: `fetch-brand-data.sh` is `curl | jq` and adds a `jq` dependency for something any agent does natively. `download-brand-assets.sh` is actively harmful right now — it downloads the live SVGs into `assets/logos/` next to same-named PNGs from the zip, silently producing a mixed-provenance folder. SKILL.md invokes `fetch-brand-data.sh` in three places (lines 56, 132, 152), so those need to become plain URL pointers.

The Python adherence checker is a different animal and I'd keep it, but see my question below.

**4. `liatrio-design-system.md:7-8` provenance block — agree, remove.**

`temp/Liatrio Design System/` doesn't exist in this repo, so it's a dangling citation. "Trust level: high" is the document grading itself. The one fact worth keeping — these are design recipes, not production components — already appears twice more, in `liatrio-component-recipes.md` under "Production-component caveat" and again in `liatrio-design-system.md` under "Known conflicts."

**5. Source priority — confirmed conflict, and the ladder itself is upside down.**

There are two competing ladders: `SKILL.md` puts the live JSON at position 4 of 4, `liatrio-design-system.md` puts it at 3 of 4, and `liatrio-asset-index.md` implies a third ordering. But the deeper problem is that both rank the self-updating live source *below* a snapshot copied out of a zip.

I think the real fix is to stop treating them as competing. They cover different ground and barely overlap. `liatrio.ai` is authoritative for palette, typography, logo inventory, icon set, and usage rules. The design system is authoritative for everything the site doesn't specify: dark-first posture, spacing and radius scales, motion, component recipes, voice and copy, motifs. Define that once in SKILL.md and have the references point at it instead of restating it.

**6. DM Sans — this is the one where the audit changed the answer.**

I fetched the CSS that liatrio.ai actually ships. The production site runs a two-font system today:

```css
html, body, .font-sans { font-family: var(--font-dm-sans), DM Sans, system-ui, sans-serif }
h1,h2,h3,h4,h5,h6, .font-display { font-family: var(--font-space-grotesk), Space Grotesk, DM Sans, system-ui, sans-serif }
```

DM Sans is not "older brand material." It is the current body font of liatrio.ai. The zip also ships DM Sans roman and italic variable fonts in `uploads/`, meaning the brand team handed them over during the design system build.

Meanwhile `brand-data.json` (lastUpdated 2026-04-14) documents Space Grotesk as the only typeface, and the zip is emphatic: "Space Grotesk is the only typeface... Hierarchy comes from size and weight, not from mixing families."

So the accurate statement is that the documented standard is Space Grotesk only, and the liatrio.ai implementation hasn't caught up. Both authoritative documents agree, so Space Grotesk-only stays the rule — but the "legacy" provenance claim is factually wrong and should be one accurate sentence instead. This matters practically: if someone points this skill at liatrio.ai's own code, the current wording tells the agent to flag the production site as stale, which is a confusing finding to hand a designer.

The mentions needing edits are SKILL.md:65/131/142, `liatrio-design-system.md`:60/116, `liatrio-component-recipes.md`:214, the evals doc at 16/41/74, the checker's `stale_dm_sans` message, and `assets/previews/type-body.html`.

**7. examples/evals — agree on placement, split verdict on value.**

Nothing in the skill loads `examples/`. The folder is referenced exactly once, by a path inside the eval doc itself.

The HTML artifact has real value, but only as the adherence checker's test fixture — and its actual consumer is `scripts/test_liatrio_design_system.py` at the repo root, not the skill. The markdown has two problems: it's human/CI QA collateral shipping inside a skill package that every consumer downloads, and its assertions are a third copy of rules that already live in SKILL.md. It has already drifted — it asserts a flat "avoids DM Sans" in one eval while asserting that audits should permit legacy DM Sans evidence in another.

## Things you didn't ask about that the cross-surface audit turned up

**Three of your logo files are the same file.** `logo_Liatrio_reverse-color.png`, `logo_Liatrio_reverse.png`, and `logo_Liatrio_reverse_preferred.png` are byte-identical, md5 `220a292e...`. `liatrio-asset-index.md` lines 63-65 gives each a distinct use case ("alternate reverse mark for cases that need the non-color reverse treatment," "preferred alternate reverse mark when a layout calls for it"). That differentiation is invented. On liatrio.ai, Reverse Color and Reverse White are genuinely different files.

**The skill is missing four logomark variants and every SVG.** `brand-data.json` lists 8 logo/logomark assets; I confirmed all 8 resolve at `https://www.liatrio.ai/brand-logos/*.svg` with HTTP 200. The skill has only zip PNGs — no black logo, no square logomark, no reverse logomark, no black logomark. The square logomark (`logomark_Liatrio_background`) exists specifically to solve "logomark on a green background," which the skill states as a prohibition in four places without ever offering the fix.

**Two previews and one motif have no source.** `assets/previews/brand-circuit-divider.html`, `assets/previews/brand-textures.html`, and `assets/motifs/circuit-divider.svg` don't exist in the zip and have no live-site counterpart — they were authored during the skill build. **The capsule-vs-square button conflict is resolvable right now.** `liatrio-design-system.md:66` and `liatrio-component-recipes.md:60` both hedge on this. The evidence is one-sided: the bundle's own `preview/components-buttons.html` ships `border-radius: 6px`, and liatrio.ai ships `--radius: 0.5rem` with buttons at `rounded-md`, which computes to 6px. Only the zip README's prose claims capsules are "our most recognisable component shape." Buttons are 6px; capsules are for pills, badges, and eyebrow chips. The hedging can go.

## Questions

I'm noticing the bundle preview is using colors like `#A3E635` and `rgba(166,239,57,0.9)` that don't appear in the brand palette—these are pulled directly from the live site. The adherence checker would flag these as unapproved values, which is worth documenting. Now I'm ready to structure my response.

I'll organize this into three parts: first, I'll address each of the seven feedback items with evidence for agreement or disagreement; second, I'll lay out the cross-surface discrepancies that need resolving; and third, I'll ask clarifying questions about the decisions ahead. Since this involves multiple trade-offs and ambiguities, I should use questions to surface the key decisions rather than making assumptions about what matters most.

Starting with the feedback items: on the PNG removal, I agree it's outdated and lower priority. But on the liatrio-brand-guidelines.md file, I need to push back — it's mislabeled as legacy when it's actually current. The icon list matches the live brand site exactly (120 Lucide icons verified), the color tables align with brand-data.json, and the Components and Spacing sections are the only documentation of the live brand site's component inventory that brand-data.json doesn't capture. Only three sections are actually stale: the DM Sans typography, the liatrio.com URLs, and the "Legacy" framing itself. My recommendation is to keep the content, strip the legacy label, update URLs to liatrio.ai, relocate the typography section, rename it to something like `references/liatrio-brand-site.md`, and treat it as a current sibling source rather than a deprecated tier.

Removing the PNG also means cleaning up references in asset-index.md at lines 17 and 85, plus SKILL.md at lines 33 and 166.

On the Implementation Decision Format, I agree it doesn't belong — it's a report about work rather than the work itself, which forces the agent into narration mode instead of building. The adherence checker enforces Brand Audit fields but nothing validates this format, and its five bullets just duplicate what's already in the Workflow Checklist and Verification Loop. I'd delete it entirely, but if traceability matters, add a single line to the verification loop asking to state which tokens and asset paths were used.

For the two shell scripts, I'm on board with removing both. Beyond portability concerns, `fetch-brand-data.sh` is just a simple curl piped to jq, which doesn't justify its own file.

The other script is actively problematic — it downloads SVGs from the live site and writes them into `assets/logos/` right alongside the PNGs from the zip, silently mixing sources in the same folder. SKILL.md currently calls `bash scripts/fetch-brand-data.sh` in two places (lines 56 and 132) plus the maintenance section, so I'll replace those with a direct URL pointer instead. I'm keeping `check-liatrio-design-adherence.py` though — that's a separate decision.

The provenance note in liatrio-design-system.md at lines 7-8 should go too, since `temp/Liatrio Design System/` doesn't actually exist in the repo, making that citation a broken reference.  The "Trust level: high" part is just self-assessment noise. The actual substance — that these are design recipes, not production components — already shows up twice elsewhere (in component-recipes.md and design-system.md), so I can collapse it to one location.

Now I'm seeing the real conflict: there are three different source priority ladders floating around. SKILL.md ranks live JSON as tier 4 (lowest), design-system.md ranks it as tier 3, and asset-index.md plus other parts of SKILL.md imply local assets should come first. The bigger issue is that both ladders place the live liatrio.ai JSON *below* a local snapshot copied from a zip file, and brand-data.json shows a lastUpdated timestamp of 2026-04-14.

The solution is to define a single source priority ladder in SKILL.md and reference it elsewhere instead of restating it. The ladder should be: liatrio.ai/brand-data.json and /brand as canonical for palette, typography, logos, icons, and usage rules; local design-system references and assets as canonical for everything the site doesn't specify (dark-first approach, spacing, radius, elevation, motion, component recipes, voice, motifs); and never use liatrio.com. These sources are complementary rather than competing, which dissolves most of the conflict.

Now I'm digging into the DM Sans audit — I pulled the actual CSS from liatrio.ai's production site.

The site currently runs a two-font system: DM Sans for body text and Space Grotesk for headings, with DM Sans as the fallback. But brand-data.json from April 2026 documents only Space Grotesk as the typeface and emphasizes it's the only one, while the brand kit itself ships both DM Sans and Space Grotesk variable fonts, suggesting the brand team intentionally included both.

So the accurate framing is: the documented standard is Space Grotesk only, but liatrio.ai's implementation uses DM Sans for body text. The skill should keep Space Grotesk as the authoritative rule, but I need to replace the "legacy" claim with a more accurate statement about the implementation gap. This is important for audit mode—flagging the production site as stale would be confusing when it's actually just lagging behind the documented standard.

I've identified several places to update: SKILL.md at lines 65, 131, and 142; design-system.md at lines 60 and 116; component-recipes.md at line 214; and multiple eval files.

Now looking at the examples folder placement and value. The folder structure is odd since nothing actually loads from `examples/` and the skill doesn't reference it except in one eval doc path. The HTML fixture has real utility as a test fixture for the checker, but it's sitting in `examples/evals/` while its only consumer is the test script at repo root. The eval markdown file with prompts and assertions is more of a human/CI QA artifact than a skill resource, which raises questions about whether it belongs here.

The core issue is that shipping test collateral inside the skill package means every consumer downloads unnecessary test files. Plus the assertions duplicate the rules already documented in SKILL.md, creating a third copy that's already drifting—it treats "avoid DM Sans" as a flat rule while the assertions allow legacy evidence. Better to move both files to the repo's test area alongside the test script, or delete the markdown and keep just the HTML fixture.

I'm also noticing some additional findings beyond what was raised: there are three identical logo files that seem redundant. The skill is also missing four logomark variants and all SVG files—the brand data references eight logo assets available on liatrio.ai, but the shipped package only contains PNG versions and lacks the black logo, square logomark (designed for green backgrounds), reverse logomark, and black logomark variants. Additionally, three preview files and one motif were created during the skill build with no source on the live site or in the original zip. The design system and component docs hedge on button styling, but the actual bundle and liatrio.ai both use 6px border-radius consistently—so that's the rule to enforce, with capsules reserved only for pills and badges. I should remove the ambiguous language and clarify this. There's also an issue with off-palette color values appearing in the preview files, like Tailwind lime-400 showing up where it shouldn't. The icon guidance needs to be updated to reflect that liatrio.ai/brand now maintains a definitive 120-icon Lucide inventory that the site actively uses, making this a concrete requirement rather than an open question. `colors_and_type.css` is a modified version with stripped comments and reflowed sections, so it'll always show diffs against a fresh bundle. The deck template exceeds the pre-commit size limit, leaving the skill's deck task mode without an actual asset. The OpenAI agent configuration is just a placeholder and should be regenerated using the scripts referenced in AGENTS.md.

I'm narrowing down the key decisions that actually need input: how to frame DM Sans usage, whether to delete or refactor the brand guidelines markdown, what to do with the evals content, whether to pull logo SVGs directly from the live site, whether to elevate the live JSON as the primary source, whether to keep the adherence checker, and whether to remove the unsourced preview assets. That's six solid questions to present.

I'm confident about recommending the source priority shift as a complementary approach rather than a competing one, but it's still worth asking since it involves some judgment. Now I'll write this up in readable prose with minimal structure—thorough enough for a full audit but keeping it tight and not overdone.

content.text:
So this is a masterclass in what not to do—white text on white background making it completely unreadable, paired with a rainbow gradient hero section, magenta buttons with yellow text that clash terribly, and a logo that's been rotated, skewed, and hue-shifted into oblivion. The copy hits every corporate cliché in the book: "leverage," "synergistic," "AI-powered," "resources," "upskill," "implementation"—all the banned vocabulary. The headline is crammed into 11px all-caps, and the call-to-action is the generic "Learn more."

The validator returns a warning rather than a failure because it's checking for the *presence* of approved tokens and hex values in the CSS, not whether they're actually being used. The dark surface check passes because `#1a1f23` appears somewhere in the style block, and the green check passes because `#24ae1d` is defined—but neither is necessarily applied to anything meaningful. The core issue is that the checks are just substring matching against the raw CSS, not semantic validation of what's actually styled. The commit message claims it evaluates styling from CSS evidence, but it's really just looking for whether the right hex codes exist anywhere in the file.

Since the exit code is 0 (warn, not fail), this passes CI even though it's backwards—it fails legitimate artifacts and passes unsafe ones. Looking at what it *does* catch: emoji and exclamation marks are genuine regex checks, DM Sans presence is real, unresolved token references are genuinely useful. But contrast checking doesn't exist in the code at all despite being part of the verification loop, and checks like "is this dark-first" or "proper hierarchy" are either unenforceable or fundamentally wrong. So there are maybe four mechanical checks worth keeping and five that are either broken or actively misleading.

Now for the duplication question—whether to embed everything in the skill or have it fetch from the website. The tradeoff hinges on availability: skills run in environments with and without network access, so hard-depending on a fetch degrades offline. Every byte in SKILL.md loads every time, while reference files load on demand and assets don't load at all.

The real risk is drift—duplicated content silently goes stale, which is already happening with the DM Sans framing being four months out of date. But brand-data.json is only 11 KB and fully machine-readable, so an agent can fetch and parse it cheaply in one call. The key insight is that palette hexes are stable, the icon list is a curated inventory that could grow, and logo inventory changes rarely.

The solution is a three-tier split based on change rate and cost of being wrong: inline only the small, stable, decision-driving values that an agent needs to make a correct choice without loading anything—like the dark canvas hex. the icon inventory is actually stuck behind a hashed filename that changes on deploy, so it's not accessible through brand-data.json the way logos and colors are. That makes a local copy genuinely necessary — it's the one piece of website content that can't be reliably fetched programmatically.

So the principle becomes clear: pull what's in brand-data.json (colors, logos, typography, guidelines), keep locally what's only in the site's JS bundles (icons, components, spacing), and maintain the brand foundations that exist nowhere else (voice, motion, posture, recipes). For the asset binaries themselves, that's a separate question about whether to duplicate them or just reference the source.

content.text:
## Checker audit

Verdict up front: it doesn't work, and the way it fails is worse than not having it. I'd move it out of the skill and either fix it hard or drop it.

Here's the test that settles it. I wrote a deliberately hostile artifact — white text on a white background, a rainbow gradient hero, a magenta CTA with yellow text, a logo rotated 37° and skewed and hue-rotated, an 11px all-caps headline, and copy stuffed with every word the brand guide bans ("leverage our synergistic AI-powered resources… upskill your people and drive implementation"), ending in a "Learn more" CTA:

```text
STATUS: warn
 warn raw_hex_color | #00ffff, #ff00ff, #ff8800, #ffff00, #ffffff
 warn raw_px_value  | 11px, 4px, 999px
```

It passes. Exit code 0. In CI that's green.

The reason is the core defect: `dark_first_surfaces` and `approved_green_tokens` are satisfied by the *presence of a substring* anywhere in a style block, not by anything being styled. My probe declares `--bg: #1a1f23` and `--accent: #24ae1d` in `:root` and never uses either one — the body is `#ffffff`. Both checks pass because `#1a1f23` and `#24ae1d` appear in the text. Same for `space_grotesk_required`: declaring the family satisfies it even though nothing inherits it. Commit 57008d0's message says it now evaluates "styling from CSS evidence instead of prose," but it still evaluates string presence, just in a narrower string.

The noise runs in the opposite direction. Every legitimate asset in the skill trips warnings:

| Checked file | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `assets/colors_and_type.css` | warn — `raw_hex_color` on `#003d5c`, `#006989`, `#00c1db`, `#2a3036`… |
| `assets/previews/colors-brand.html` | warn ×4 |
| `assets/previews/components-buttons.html` | warn ×4 |
| `examples/evals/representative-dark-html-artifact.html` | **pass, 0 findings, 0 warnings** |

It flags the canonical token definition file for containing raw hex — that file is where raw hex is supposed to live, it's the thing that defines the tokens. It flags every preview card for `missing_main_region` and `missing_title`, but preview cards are fragments by design. And `raw_px_value` fires on any px in an authored style block, which means it can never be satisfied: the design system's spacing and type scales *are* px values, so a perfectly faithful implementation always warns.

Meanwhile the one artifact that passes clean is the fixture written alongside the checker. That's circular — the test proves the fixture matches the checker, not that either matches the brand.

There's also a scope mismatch worth flagging. `SKILL.md`'s verification loop and the eval doc both lean on contrast checking, and the checker computes no contrast at all — there's no luminance or ratio math anywhere in the 308 lines. My white-on-white probe is the proof.

What's actually salvageable is small but real: emoji detection, exclamation marks, DM Sans presence, and `unresolved_token_reference` (catching `var(--foo)` with no definition, which genuinely finds broken artifacts). Those four are mechanically checkable and the checker gets them right. Everything else is either unenforceable by regex — is this dark-first, is the hierarchy deliberate, does this pass contrast — or actively inverted.

So my recommendation: move it to repo `scripts/` alongside `test_liatrio_design_system.py`, strip it to the four checks that work, and drop the pretense that it validates design-system adherence. Rename it to something honest like `check-artifact-hygiene.py`. If you'd rather not spend the time, deleting it costs you almost nothing — a skill that tells an agent "verify contrast and token usage" gets better results than one that hands the agent a tool which green-lights white-on-white.

## The duplication question

This is the right thing to be worried about, and there's a clean line to draw. It's not "website vs skill" — it's **what is programmatically fetchable**.

I checked, and `brand-data.json` contains exactly five keys: `meta`, `logos`, `typography`, `colors`, `guidelines`. It has **no icons section, no components section, and no spacing section.** Those three tabs exist on `liatrio.ai/brand` but they're rendered client-side from `/_next/static/chunks/app/brand/page-<hash>.js` — and that hash changes on every deploy. I only got the icon list by fetching the current chunk and regexing it. An agent cannot reliably retrieve that.

That gives you three tiers with a real test behind each:

**Fetchable — don't duplicate, point at the URL.** The full color palette with RGB and CMYK, the logo and logomark file inventory with exact paths, the typography spec, and the four guideline blurbs. All of it is in an 11 KB JSON one fetch away. This is the content currently duplicated across `references/liatrio-brand-guidelines.md` and partially into `liatrio-design-system.md`, and it's the duplication that has the highest drift risk because it looks authoritative while being a snapshot.

**On the site but not fetchable — keep locally, it's the only copy.** The 120-icon Lucide inventory, the component variant inventory (button variants and sizes and states, badge variants, card types, form states, alert types), and the spacing/radius/shadow token names. This is precisely the content in the file you wanted to delete, and it's the strongest argument for refactoring rather than deleting it. It's about 2 KB of text.

**Not on the site at all — keep locally, sole record.** Dark-first posture, the spacing and radius scales with usage rules, motion and easing, hover/press/focus behavior, component recipes, layering and motifs, and the entire voice and copy section. None of this exists on liatrio.ai in any form. It's not duplication; it's the only place it's written down.

Applied to your specific question about the refactored brand-site reference: it shrinks a lot. Drop its color tables and logo tables entirely — replace with a pointer to `brand-data.json` and a one-line note on what keys it contains. Drop the typography section. Keep the icons, components, and spacing sections. The file goes from ~12 KB to roughly 3 KB and stops competing with the live source.

For `SKILL.md` itself, I'd inline only the handful of values that drive a decision before any file gets loaded — `#1A1F23`, `#1E2327`, `#24AE1D`, `#89DF00`, Space Grotesk, and the 4.5:1 / 3:1 ratios. Six facts that haven't changed and won't change independently of everything else. Everything else becomes a pointer.

**Binaries are a separate calculus,** and here duplication wins outright. "Static/offline artifact" is an explicit task mode, and you can't inline a logo from a URL into a self-contained HTML file. The good news is it's nearly free: all 8 canonical SVGs total **16.6 KB**, versus **243 KB** for the current 7 PNGs, three of which are byte-identical to each other. So committing the SVGs gets you four more variants, resolution independence, and a 93% size reduction. Ship all 8 SVGs, drop the PNGs, and point to `liatrio.ai/brand-logos/` in the reference for anyone who wants the PNG renders.

One consequence worth naming before I start: this means `liatrio-design-system.md` should stop restating the color palette in its token quick-reference table, since that table duplicates `brand-data.json`. ---
name: liatrio-brand-guidelines
description: "Applies Liatrio brand and design-system guidance for UI design, docs, decks, brand audits, asset selection, typography, visual polish, and formal compliance checks. Use when users request Liatrio styling, implementation decisions, static/offline artifacts, hero/social imagery, or design-system adherence review."
license: Apache-2.0
metadata:
  owner: liatrio
  compatibility: Designed for skills-compatible coding agents with markdown reading. Optional network access improves accuracy by verifying the current live brand-data source.
  canonical-brand-source: https://www.liatrio.ai/brand-data.json
---

# Liatrio Brand and Design-System Router

## When to Use

Use this skill when the user asks for any of the following:

- Liatrio-branded UI implementation, static HTML, documentation, decks, screenshots, or social/hero imagery.
- Brand audits, compliance reviews, accessibility checks, and corrective design-system recommendations.
- Logo, logomark, motif, preview, typography, color, spacing, component, or asset-selection decisions.
- Visual polish for existing artifacts that should match the current Liatrio design system.
- Resolving stale or conflicting Liatrio brand guidance in code, docs, slides, or generated assets.

## Core Facts

These six hold for every Liatrio surface. Everything else, load on demand.

- Dark canvas `#1A1F23`; elevated cards and panels `#1E2327`.
- Primary Green `#24AE1D` is the hero color for key brand moments.
- Bright Green `#89DF00` is the highlight, used sparingly and never as a dominant fill.
- Space Grotesk is the only typeface. Hierarchy comes from size and weight, not family.
- Contrast floors: 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text and non-text UI.
- Sentence case everywhere. ALL CAPS only for eyebrow labels at 14px or smaller.

## Two Authoritative Sources

The live brand site and the local design system cover different ground. They are
complementary, not competing — check the one that owns the question.

**`https://www.liatrio.ai/brand-data.json` owns** the color palette (HEX, RGB, CMYK),
the typography specification, the logo and logomark inventory with file paths, and the
four published usage guidelines. Fetch it directly when a task needs exact values,
print-ready CMYK, the full logo inventory, or confirmation that the guideline has not
changed since the `2026-04-14` stamp this skill was written against. Do not copy its
contents into artifacts as if they were skill-local guidance.

**The local references own** everything the site does not publish: dark-first visual
posture, spacing and radius scales, motion and easing, hover/press/focus behavior,
component recipes, layering and motif rules, and voice and copy conventions. These
exist nowhere else.

Three narrower rules follow from that split:

- The site's Icons, Components, and Spacing tabs are rendered from a hashed JS bundle
  and cannot be fetched reliably. They are recorded in `references/liatrio-brand-site.md`.
- `liatrio.com` is dead as a source. Never fetch it and never cite it as canonical.
- If network access is unavailable, work from local references and assets and say
  plainly that live verification was not performed.

When a genuine conflict appears, name it explicitly rather than silently picking a side.

## Task-Mode Routing

Identify the request mode, then load only the references and assets that mode needs.

- `implementation`: direct UI/docs/style changes. Load `references/liatrio-design-system.md` and `references/liatrio-component-recipes.md` before choosing tokens, type, layout, and motifs.
- `audit`: compliance findings. Preserve the Brand Audit output contract below, cite the specific sources checked, and give proof for contrast, typography, source freshness, and asset choices.
- `design-system implementation`: a current Liatrio design-system surface. Space Grotesk, dark-first graphite surfaces, green signal accents, flat technical components, botanical and texture motifs, local preview recipes.
- `static/offline artifact`: a portable static file, screenshot, or helper output. Use bundled local fonts and assets; avoid remote runtime dependencies unless the user allows them.
- `deck`: slides or presentation guidance. Use curated deck assets when present, confirm logo and background fit, apply the same accessibility checks as UI work.
- `social/hero image`: visual or image direction. Confirm dimensions and background brightness, pick the right logo variant, choose motifs deliberately rather than decoratively.

## Quick Start Workflow

1. Determine the task mode.
2. Confirm output surface, audience, dimensions, background brightness, and whether offline/local-only behavior is required.
3. Load the targeted local references and assets rather than expanding this router into a full token catalog.
4. If exact values or freshness matter and network is allowed, fetch `https://www.liatrio.ai/brand-data.json` and record that you checked it.
5. Apply the rules, confirm asset choices, run accessibility checks, and work the verification loop before final output.

## Core Rules

### Typography

- Space Grotesk for everything: display, headlines, body, UI labels, table cells.
- Weights: 300 for large editorial quotes, 400 for body, 500 for buttons and eyebrows and table headers, 600 for H2/H3/display, 700 for H1 only.
- Use the bundled font at `assets/fonts/SpaceGrotesk-VariableFont_wght.ttf` for offline artifacts rather than calling Google Fonts.
- Reserve a monospace stack for code, version tags, and technical labels.
- liatrio.ai currently ships DM Sans for body text while its headings use Space Grotesk. The published guideline says Space Grotesk throughout, and the guideline governs. Treat DM Sans as expected when auditing liatrio.ai's own code and as a defect anywhere else.

### Colors and Visual Posture

- Dark-first: `#1A1F23` canvas, `#1E2327` elevated cards. Light surfaces (`#FFFFFF` / `#F8F9FA`) are for deliberate editorial breaks, print, and product screenshots.
- One expressive accent per surface. Primary Green for hero moments, Bright Green for highlights, Violet as the editorial counterpoint at most once per surface.
- Status colors are reserved and semantic: Lagoon `#00C1DB` for info, Hot Red `#E63946` for errors, Flame Orange `#F77F00` for warnings. Never decorative.
- Hairline borders before shadows on dark. Flat technical cards, structured grids, restrained shadows, green glow only for active brand moments.
- For the full palette with RGB and CMYK, fetch the live brand data rather than guessing.

### Logo, Asset, and Motif Usage

- Maintain clear space around the logo equal to the height of the `L` in `liatrio`.
- Never distort, rotate, recolor, or place logos on low-contrast backgrounds.
- Horizontal lockups are primary; stacked variants are secondary and only for square or near-square placements.
- The standard logomark must not sit on a green background. Use `logomark_Liatrio_background.svg` (the square variant) or a reverse variant instead.
- Pick logo variants by background brightness and state the exact asset path you used.
- Layer botanical and texture motifs over the dark base only when they support the content hierarchy.

### Copy and Accessibility

- Confident, technical, low-fluff copy in sentence case. Default to `we` for Liatrio and `you` or `your team` for the reader.
- No emoji and no exclamation marks in marketing or product UI copy unless the user explicitly asks for a different tone.
- Meet the contrast floors above. Do not rely on color alone for status; add text, icon, or structure.
- Provide alt text for logos, motifs, and meaningful imagery. Hide decorative textures from assistive tech.

## Output Contract

### Brand Audit Format

Use this exact structure for brand and design-system audits:

```markdown
## Brand Audit

- Scope: [screens/files/components reviewed]
- Compliant: [what matches Liatrio standards]
- Issues: [specific mismatches with source references]
- Fixes: [exact token, typography, layout, copy, and asset substitutions]
- Verification: [contrast/logo/background/type/source checks performed]
- Source Validation: [local references/assets checked and live liatrio.ai JSON checked or not checked]
```

## Verification Loop

Before finalizing, run this loop:

1. Draft the recommendation, audit, or implementation choices.
2. Load the targeted reference for the task mode and compare exact token, type, component, and asset choices against it.
3. Confirm Space Grotesk is the typeface in every brand-facing artifact.
4. State the exact tokens and asset paths used, so the choice can be reviewed.
5. Confirm logo, logomark, motif, and preview assets match background brightness, hierarchy, and offline requirements.
6. Verify contrast, focus states, alt text, and non-color-only semantics.
7. If exact values or freshness mattered, say whether the live brand data was fetched. Report any source conflicts or missing assets.

## Workflow Checklist

- [ ] Identify task mode: implementation, audit, design-system implementation, static/offline artifact, deck, or social/hero image.
- [ ] Confirm surface, background context, audience, dimensions, and offline/runtime constraints.
- [ ] Load only the targeted local references and assets needed for the mode.
- [ ] Apply Space Grotesk throughout.
- [ ] Choose dark-first surfaces, Primary Green for key actions, Bright Green only as a signal highlight.
- [ ] Select logo, logomark, and motif assets by exact path and explain the choice.
- [ ] Verify contrast ratios, focus states, non-color-only semantics, and alt text.
- [ ] Check copy for technical tone, sentence case, no emoji, and no unnecessary exclamation marks.
- [ ] State whether live brand data was fetched and note any conflicts.

## References

- `references/liatrio-design-system.md` — visual posture, token roles, type scale, spacing, motion, copy rules.
- `references/liatrio-component-recipes.md` — implementation recipes for heroes, cards, buttons, chips, forms, dividers, and compositions.
- `references/liatrio-asset-index.md` — which bundled asset to use for which job, and what to avoid.
- `references/liatrio-brand-site.md` — the Lucide icon inventory, component variant surface, and site spacing tokens that the live JSON does not expose.
- `assets/colors_and_type.css` — local token CSS.
- `assets/logos/`, `assets/motifs/`, `assets/previews/`, `assets/fonts/` — curated local assets.
- `https://www.liatrio.ai/brand-data.json` — live canonical palette, typography, logo inventory, and usage guidelines.

This file owns what the live brand site does not publish: visual posture, token roles,
spacing and motion, and copy conventions. For exact palette values, CMYK, or the logo
file inventory, fetch `https://www.liatrio.ai/brand-data.json` instead of reading them
here.

## Visual posture

Liatrio is **dark-first, high-contrast, technical-but-organic**. The signature look is
a cool graphite surface with precise technical UI structure, bright green signal
accents, and botanical or textured detail as the organic counterpoint.

- Default canvas: `#1A1F23` (`--dark-bg`).
- Elevated/card surface: `#1E2327` (`--dark-bg-2`).
- Structure: flat technical surfaces, hairline borders, compact labels, strong grid rhythm, very restrained shadows.
- Signature motif: dark base, low-opacity hex or trace texture, green trace detail, then a Liatris botanical image or the three-pillar Venn diagram.
- Light surfaces are allowed for editorial breaks, printable assets, product screenshots, and deck pages, but they do not replace the dark-first default.

## Token roles

The design system's contribution is the **role assignment** — which color does which
job. The values below are the ones you need in hand to make a choice; the authoritative
palette, including RGB and CMYK, lives in the live brand data.

| Role | Token | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dark canvas | `--dark-bg` | Default page, hero, product surface background |
| Dark elevated | `--dark-bg-2` | Cards, panels, form fields, section contrast |
| Primary green | `--primary-green` | Hero brand moments, primary CTA, focus rings |
| Bright green | `--bright-green` | Highlights, active borders, links, callouts, trace detail |
| Lime | `--lime` | Enablement pillar, square chips, editorial counterpoint |
| Violet | `--violet` | Strategy pillar, one-per-surface editorial counterpoint |
| Lagoon | `--lagoon` | Info states, secondary data visuals |
| Hot red | `--hot-red` | Errors and alerts only |
| Flame orange | `--flame-orange` | Warnings only |
| Foreground ramp | `--fg`, `--fg-muted`, `--fg-subtle`, `--fg-faint` | Five foreground levels instead of opacity stacks |
| Border | `--border`, `--border-strong` | Hairline structure, used before shadows |

Rules of thumb:

- One expressive accent per surface. Do not decorate with the full palette.
- Bright green is a signal, not a page fill.
- Lagoon, red, and orange are semantic. They each have a job; do not borrow them for decoration.
- Avoid warm, grainy, generic stock-photo treatments.

Concrete values are defined once, in `../assets/colors_and_type.css`. Import that file
rather than restating hex codes, and use raw hex only in standalone artifacts where the
token CSS cannot be included.

## Typography

Space Grotesk is the typeface. Hierarchy comes from size and weight, never from mixing
families.

- **Font stack:** `"Space Grotesk", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif`.
- **Weights:** 300 for large quotes and editorial body, 400 for paragraphs, 500 for buttons and eyebrows and table headers, 600 for H2/H3/display, 700 for H1 only.
- **Scale:** display 60px; H1 48-60px; H2 36-40px; H3 28-32px; H4 22px; body 16-18px; small 14px; micro 12px; eyebrow 13px at `0.14em` tracking.
- **Tracking:** `-0.02em` for large headlines, default for body. Uppercase only for small technical eyebrows and chips.
- **Mono:** reserve `ui-monospace`, JetBrains Mono, SF Mono, Menlo, or Consolas for code, version tags, technical labels, and token names.

## Spacing, radii, layout, and elevation

- **Spacing:** 4px base scale — 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128. Component padding clusters at 16/24/32, section padding at 64/96/128.
- **Radii:** `--r-1` 4px for inputs and code chips, `--r-2` 8px for small controls, `--r-3` 12px for cards, `--r-4` 16px for large surfaces, `--r-5` 24px for hero panels, `--r-pill` 999px for pills, badges, and eyebrow chips.
- **Button radius:** 6px. The design system's own button preview ships `border-radius: 6px` and liatrio.ai renders buttons at `rounded-md`, which computes to 6px against its `--radius: 0.5rem` base. Both agree. Capsules are for pills, badges, and eyebrow chips — not for buttons.
- **Grid:** 12 columns, roughly 80px desktop gutters and 24px mobile, max content width around 1280px, editorial reading width around 720px.
- **Elevation:** borders first on dark surfaces. Shadows are for floating UI — menus, modals, toasts. Green glow marks active or focused brand moments.

## Motion and interaction

- Default easing: `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`.
- Durations: 120ms micro and hover, 200ms state changes, 320ms panel and modal, 600ms page-level reveals.
- No bounces or springy overshoots. The brand is precise.
- Fades enter from below with 8-16px translate-Y, never from the side.
- Hover: green elements gain a subtle glow or outline and can translate `Y(-1px)`; dark surfaces lighten about 6%.
- Press: scale to about `0.98` and drop the glow. No color shift.
- Focus: visible 2px bright-green outline at 2px offset. Never the browser default.
- The flame logomark is the one expressive exception — it may flicker, rotate, morph, or render in 3D as a hero moment.

## Iconography

Lucide, confirmed. The brand site publishes a curated 120-icon inventory and renders
Lucide throughout, so this is a brand decision rather than a substitution. The full list
is in `liatrio-brand-site.md`. Do not mix icon families.

The flame logomark serves as the brand icon for favicons, loaders, and deck corners.
The Venn diagram is an infographic device, not an icon. Botanical imagery is
large-format only.

Unicode glyphs sparingly — `→` for inline CTAs is fine, decorative glyphs are not.

## Copy rules

- Voice: confident, technical, low-fluff, a senior engineer who is also good at strategy.
- Person: `we` for Liatrio, `you` or `your team` for the reader. Avoid `I` in brand work and `the client` in client-facing copy.
- Casing: sentence case for headlines, buttons, and navigation. Title Case only for proper product names. ALL CAPS only for small tracked labels.
- Punctuation: no exclamation marks in marketing or product UI. Em dashes are welcome. Oxford commas.
- Numbers: numerals for 2 and above; spell out `one`.
- Prefer: ship, build, scale, engineering team, enablement, pilot, rollout, AI-first, teach your team.
- Avoid: leverage, synergize, resources, overused `upskilling`, vague `implementation`, default `AI-powered`, and `train your people` where `teach your team` is clearer.
- CTAs are verb-led and specific: `Start a pilot` over `Get started`, `Talk to an engineer` over `Contact us`.
- Emoji: not in marketing copy or product UI, and never as an icon substitute.

## Logo and motif rules

- Horizontal full-color is primary on light backgrounds; horizontal reverse-color is primary on dark.
- Stacked variants are secondary, for square or near-square placements only.
- The flame logomark works as favicon, app icon, deck corner, or loader. It must not sit on a green background — use the square logomark variant there.
- Maintain clear space equal to the height of the `L` in `liatrio`.
- Never distort, rotate, recolor, stretch, or add effects to logo files.
- The three-pillar Venn canonically represents Build, Strategy, and Enablement. Use it as a section or infographic motif, not as tiny decorative noise.
- Botanical Liatris imagery is a large-format motif; do not shrink it to icon size.

## Accessibility and review checks

- Normal text contrast: at least 4.5:1. Large text and non-text UI: at least 3:1.
- Primary Green on white passes large-text only. Use Grey 800 for body copy on light surfaces.
- Do not rely on color alone for status; add a label, icon, position, or text.
- Provide alt text for images and logos. Hide decorative textures from assistive tech.
- Ensure keyboard focus is visible on every interactive element.
- Keep body copy legible over botanical or gradient imagery using a protection gradient or dark overlay.

## Caveats

- The design system was built from the brand guideline document without a production codebase or Figma source attached. Treat the preview cards as design recipes, not pixel-perfect production components. This caveat is stated once here and once in `liatrio-component-recipes.md`; it does not need repeating in output.
- `_ds_bundle.js` in the source bundle initializes a namespace for previews and exports no reusable component API. It is not shipped with this skill and should not be referenced.

## Provenance

Assets come from two places, and the distinction matters when refreshing them:

Stacked logo lockups are the one exception: they exist in the design-system bundle but

Logo rules:

- Clear space equal to the height of the `L` in `liatrio`.
- Horizontal lockups are primary; stacked variants are secondary.
- Provide alt text unless the logo is decorative and redundant with adjacent text.
- PNG renders of every variant are available at the same paths on `liatrio.ai` with a `.png` extension if a consumer cannot handle SVG.

## Motif, background, and infographic assets

| Asset | Background | Use case | Avoid |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `liatris-digital.png` | Dark, with protection gradient | Signature botanical counterpoint in heroes, social cards, deck covers | Do not shrink to icon size; it is not an icon. |
| `venn-diagram.png` | Dark or light with sufficient contrast | Build · Strategy · Enablement infographic, deck section marker | Do not use as a tiny decorative icon; label or explain it. |

| `liatris-violet.png` (~2.3 MB), `liatrio-bg01.png` (~1.3 MB), `liatrio-bg08.png` (~584 KB) | Same size policy | Use `liatris-digital.png` and the SVG textures, or request an approved external path for large editorial imagery. |

Preview cards are byte-for-byte copies of the design system's review cards, except
`brand-logo.html`, `brand-imagery.html`, and `brand-venn.html`, whose asset paths were

| --- | --- |
| `_card.css` | Shared preview-card CSS dependency |
| `colors-brand.html` | Brand greens, violet and lime accents, flame gradient |
| `colors-secondary.html` | Lagoon, lime, violet, and the secondary greys |
| `colors-tertiary.html` | Extended greys, blues, hot red, flame orange |
| `colors-greys.html` | Graphite and neutral ramp guidance |
| `colors-semantic.html` | Foreground hierarchy, surfaces, border roles |
| `type-display.html`, `type-body.html`, `type-weights.html` | Space Grotesk scale, weights, body readability |
| `spacing-scale.html`, `spacing-radii.html`, `spacing-elevation.html` | Spacing steps, radius, elevation posture |
| `components-buttons.html` | Primary, outlined, foreground, and icon button recipes |
| `components-cards.html` | Flat dark card and active card treatment |
| `components-badges.html` | Pill and status label recipes |
| `components-chips-notch.html` | Square chips and the clipped-notch card shape |
| `components-forms.html` | Input, textarea, focus, error, checkbox states |
| `brand-gradient-divider.html` | Violet-to-lime hairline divider |
| `brand-venn.html` | Three-pillar Venn usage |
| `brand-imagery.html`, `brand-logo.html` | Asset treatment, motif layering, logo variant rules |

Preview guidance:

- Previews are inspection aids and recipe evidence, not production code or exported components.
- Do not embed entire preview files into always-loaded prompts.
- Two previews carry values that are not in the brand palette: `components-chips-notch.html` uses `#A3E635` and `components-buttons.html` uses `rgba(166,239,57,0.9)`. Both are near-lime approximations. Use `--lime` (`#C6F135`) or `--bright-green` (`#89DF00`) instead when implementing from these cards.

## Asset-selection workflow

1. Identify the artifact type: UI, static HTML, deck, social or hero image, audit, or implementation guidance.
2. Choose one primary brand signal: logo, botanical focal image, Venn diagram, texture, or gradient divider.
3. Confirm background compatibility — full-color logo on light, reverse-preferred on dark, protection gradient for type over imagery.
4. Check accessibility: contrast targets, alt text, no color-only status semantics.
5. For offline artifacts, copy the curated local assets into the output bundle and avoid unapproved remote fonts and images.
6. Report a missing local asset as a curation gap rather than linking to a legacy source.

## Explicit exclusions

Do not copy or depend on these:

- The original design-system ZIP, or its `uploads/`, `scratch/`, and `scraps/` directories as browsing targets. Assets promoted out of them are listed above by their new paths.
- Raw web-capture JSON or full manifest dumps.
- `_ds_bundle.js` as a component API.
- `liatrio.com` assets. That domain is dead as a source.
- Any credential, token, OAuth artifact, or private user upload.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Mechanical hygiene checks for generated Liatrio artifacts.

Scope is deliberately narrow. This checks only properties that can be decided
from the text of a file without judgment:

    - Space Grotesk is the declared typeface, and DM Sans is not.
    - Every ``var(--token)`` reference resolves to a definition the artifact can see.
    - Visible copy contains no emoji and no exclamation marks.
    - A Brand Audit uses the documented contract fields.
    - HTML does not pull remote resources at runtime.

It does NOT evaluate design-system adherence. It cannot tell whether a surface
is dark-first, whether an accent is used correctly, whether contrast passes, or
whether a layout matches the brand. Declaring a token and applying it are
indistinguishable to a regex. Use the skill's verification loop for those.

Reads only local files and uses only the standard library.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any
from urllib.parse import urlparse

CSS_IMPORT_RE = re.compile(r"@import\s+(?:url\(\s*)?[\"']([^\"']+)[\"']\s*\)?\s*;", re.IGNORECASE)
TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"var\(\s*(--[a-z0-9-]+)\s*\)", re.IGNORECASE)
TOKEN_DEFINITION_RE = re.compile(r"(--[a-z0-9-]+)\s*:\s*[^;]+;", re.IGNORECASE)
EMOJI_RE = re.compile(
    "["
    "\U0001f300-\U0001faff"
    "\U00002700-\U000027bf"
    "\U00002600-\U000026ff"
    "]"
)
AUDIT_FIELDS = ("scope", "compliant", "issues", "fixes", "verification", "source validation")


def add(items: list[dict[str, Any]], code: str, message: str, severity: str, evidence: str | None = None) -> None:
    item: dict[str, Any] = {"code": code, "severity": severity, "message": message}
    if evidence:
        item["evidence"] = evidence[:240]
    items.append(item)


def extract_visible_copy(text: str) -> str:
    text = re.sub(r"<script\b[^>]*>.*?</script>", " ", text, flags=re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
    text = re.sub(r"<style\b[^>]*>.*?</style>", " ", text, flags=re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
    text = re.sub(r"<!--.*?-->", " ", text, flags=re.DOTALL)
    text = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", text)
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()


def read_stylesheet_with_direct_imports(stylesheet: Path) -> str:
    """Read a local stylesheet plus one level of its direct local imports."""
    text = stylesheet.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    chunks = [text]
    for href in CSS_IMPORT_RE.findall(text):
        parsed = urlparse(href)
        if parsed.scheme or parsed.netloc:
            continue
        imported = (stylesheet.parent / parsed.path).resolve()
        if imported.is_file():
            chunks.append(imported.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
    return "\n".join(chunks)


def extract_style_evidence(path: Path, text: str) -> str:
    """Return CSS the artifact actually applies: inline plus linked local sheets."""
    suffix = path.suffix.lower()
    if suffix == ".css":
        return text
    if suffix not in {".html", ".htm"}:
        return ""

    chunks = re.findall(r"<style\b[^>]*>(.*?)</style>", text, flags=re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
    chunks.extend(re.findall(r"\sstyle=[\"']([^\"']*)[\"']", text, flags=re.IGNORECASE))
    for tag in re.findall(r"<link\b[^>]*>", text, flags=re.IGNORECASE):
        if not re.search(r"\brel=[\"'][^\"']*stylesheet[^\"']*[\"']", tag, flags=re.IGNORECASE):
            continue
        href_match = re.search(r"\bhref=[\"']([^\"']+)[\"']", tag, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
        if not href_match:
            continue
        parsed = urlparse(href_match.group(1))
        if parsed.scheme or parsed.netloc:
            continue
        stylesheet = (path.parent / parsed.path).resolve()
        if stylesheet.is_file():
            chunks.append(read_stylesheet_with_direct_imports(stylesheet))
    return "\n".join(chunks)


def extract_remote_runtime_refs(text: str, style_evidence: str) -> list[str]:
    """Return remote URLs loaded as resources, ignoring URLs cited as prose."""
    refs = set(re.findall(r"https?://[^\s\"'<>)]*", style_evidence, re.IGNORECASE))
    for tag, attribute in (
        ("img", "src"),
        ("script", "src"),
        ("source", "src"),
        ("video", "src"),
        ("video", "poster"),
        ("audio", "src"),
        ("object", "data"),
    ):
        refs.update(re.findall(rf"<{tag}\b[^>]*\b{attribute}=[\"'](https?://[^\"']+)[\"']", text, re.IGNORECASE))
    for tag in re.findall(r"<link\b[^>]*>", text, flags=re.IGNORECASE):
        if re.search(r"\brel=[\"'][^\"']*stylesheet[^\"']*[\"']", tag, flags=re.IGNORECASE):
            refs.update(re.findall(r"\bhref=[\"'](https?://[^\"']+)[\"']", tag, re.IGNORECASE))
    return sorted(refs)


def has_audit_field(text: str, field: str) -> bool:
    markdown_field = rf"(?im)^\s*-\s*{re.escape(field)}\s*:"
    html_field = rf"(?is)<(?:li|dt|p)\b[^>]*>\s*(?:<strong\b[^>]*>)?\s*{re.escape(field)}\s*:"
    return bool(re.search(markdown_field, text) or re.search(html_field, text))


def resolve_local_path(path_arg: str, findings: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> Path | None:
    if urlparse(path_arg).scheme:
        add(findings, "non_local_input", "Input must be a local file path, not a URL.", "error", path_arg)
        return None
    path = Path(path_arg).expanduser().resolve()
    if not path.is_file():
        add(findings, "missing_file", "File does not exist or is not a regular file.", "error", str(path))
        return None
    return path


def check(path: Path, text: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    findings: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    warnings: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    suffix = path.suffix.lower()
    style_evidence = extract_style_evidence(path, text)
    styled = suffix in {".html", ".htm", ".css"}
    is_brand_audit = bool(
        re.search(r"(?im)^\s{0,3}#{1,6}\s+brand audit\s*$", text)
        or re.search(r"<h[1-6]\b[^>]*>\s*brand audit\s*</h[1-6]>", text, re.IGNORECASE)
    )

    if styled and not is_brand_audit:
        lowered_styles = style_evidence.lower()
        if "space grotesk" not in lowered_styles:
            add(findings, "missing_space_grotesk", "No Space Grotesk declaration found in applied CSS.", "error")
        if "dm sans" in lowered_styles:
            add(
                findings,
                "dm_sans_declared",
                "DM Sans is declared. Space Grotesk is the only Liatrio typeface; DM Sans is expected only in liatrio.ai's own codebase.",
                "error",
                "DM Sans",
            )

        used = {t.lower() for t in TOKEN_RE.findall(style_evidence)}
        defined = {t.lower() for t in TOKEN_DEFINITION_RE.findall(style_evidence)}
        unresolved = sorted(used - defined)
        if unresolved:
            add(
                findings,
                "unresolved_token_reference",
                "CSS variables are referenced without a definition the artifact can see.",
                "error",
                ", ".join(unresolved[:8]),
            )

        remote = extract_remote_runtime_refs(text if suffix in {".html", ".htm"} else "", style_evidence)
        if remote:
            add(
                findings,
                "remote_runtime_resource",
                "Artifact loads remote resources at runtime; offline artifacts should bundle them locally.",
                "warning",
                ", ".join(remote[:5]),
            )
            warnings.append(findings.pop())

    visible_copy = extract_visible_copy(text)
    if EMOJI_RE.search(visible_copy):
        add(findings, "emoji_in_copy", "Emoji found in visible copy.", "error")
    exclamations = visible_copy.count("!")
    if exclamations:
        add(findings, "exclamation_in_copy", "Exclamation marks found in visible copy.", "error", f"count={exclamations}")

    if is_brand_audit:
        missing = [field for field in AUDIT_FIELDS if not has_audit_field(text, field)]
        if missing:
            add(findings, "missing_audit_structure", "Brand Audit is missing required contract fields.", "error", ", ".join(missing))

    status = "fail" if findings else ("warn" if warnings else "pass")
    return {
        "status": status,
        "checked_file": str(path),
        "findings": findings,
        "warnings": warnings,
        "summary": {
            "finding_count": len(findings),
            "warning_count": len(warnings),
            "checks": [
                "local_file_only",
                "space_grotesk_declared",
                "dm_sans_absent",
                "tokens_resolve",
                "copy_no_emoji_or_exclamation",
                "brand_audit_contract_when_applicable",
                "no_remote_runtime_resources",
            ],
            "not_checked": [
                "contrast_ratios",
                "dark_first_surfaces",
                "accent_usage",
                "layout_and_hierarchy",
            ],
        },
    }


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("artifact", help="Local file path to inspect. URLs are rejected.")
    parser.add_argument("--pretty", action="store_true", help="Pretty-print JSON output.")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    findings: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    path = resolve_local_path(args.artifact, findings)
    if path is None:
        result = {
            "status": "fail",
            "checked_file": args.artifact,
            "findings": findings,
            "warnings": [],
            "summary": {"finding_count": len(findings), "warning_count": 0, "checks": ["local_file_only"]},
        }
    else:
        result = check(path, path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))

    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2 if args.pretty else None, sort_keys=True))
    return 1 if result["status"] == "fail" else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Liatrio Design-System Representative Evals

Manual review prompts for validating the `liatrio-brand-guidelines` skill. These are QA
collateral for humans, not skill guidance — the skill itself does not load this file.

Most of what matters here needs human judgment. The mechanical subset can be checked
with `scripts/check_artifact_hygiene.py`, which verifies typography declarations, token
resolution, copy hygiene, and the Brand Audit contract. It deliberately does not judge
contrast, dark-first posture, accent usage, or layout, so a clean hygiene run is a floor
rather than a pass.

## Eval 1: Dark HTML artifact generation

**Prompt**

> Create a single-file dark-first Liatrio landing-page hero for a platform engineering
> service. Use only bundled local Liatrio skill assets and references. The output should
> be static HTML suitable for offline review.

**Check by hand**

- Dark-first surfaces: `#1A1F23` canvas with `#1E2327` cards, not a generic black.
- One expressive accent. Primary Green reserved for the hero moment; Bright Green used as a highlight rather than a fill.
- Headline at 48-60px, weight 600-700, `-0.02em` tracking, sentence case.
- Body copy contrast at or above 4.5:1 against its actual background.
- Logo variant matches background brightness, and the exact asset path is stated.
- No remote font or image requests.

**Check mechanically**

```bash
python scripts/check_artifact_hygiene.py path/to/artifact.html --pretty
```

A reference artifact that passes clean lives at
`scripts/fixtures/liatrio-representative-artifact.html`.

## Eval 2: Brand and design-system audit

**Prompt**

> Audit the provided Liatrio UI mockup or HTML artifact against the current Liatrio brand
> and design-system skill. Preserve the skill's Brand Audit output contract and include
> concrete remediation guidance.

**Check by hand**

- Findings cite specific sources rather than gesturing at "brand guidelines".
- Contrast claims include computed ratios, not assertions.
- Distinguishes what the live brand data owns from what the local design system owns.
- Remediation names exact tokens and asset paths.
- Does not flag DM Sans as a defect when the audited code is liatrio.ai's own.

**Check mechanically**

The hygiene checker enforces the six contract fields (`Scope`, `Compliant`, `Issues`,
`Fixes`, `Verification`, `Source Validation`) when a document is headed `Brand Audit`.

## Eval 3: Deck asset selection

**Prompt**

> Recommend Liatrio deck assets and layout guidance for a technical executive-readout
> deck. Use the curated local asset index and avoid assuming uncommitted assets exist.

**Check by hand**

- Logo variants chosen per slide background, with reasoning.
- Motifs used where they carry the story, not as decoration.
- Treats the PowerPoint template as an uncommitted asset to request, not a bundled file.
- References `references/liatrio-asset-index.md` and paths under `assets/`.

## Eval 4: Static and offline helper restyling

**Prompt**

> Restyle an existing static helper page so it reads as a Liatrio-branded offline
> artifact. Keep it self-contained and avoid external runtime dependencies.

**Check by hand**

- Bundled Space Grotesk via local `@font-face`, or tokens copied from `assets/colors_and_type.css`.
- Local image and logo references only, or a stated reason imagery was omitted.
- Hairline borders, flat cards, compact labels.
- No Google Fonts, CDN CSS, or remote images.

**Check mechanically**

The hygiene checker's `remote_runtime_resource` warning covers the last point.

Everything is applied, unstaged, and verified. Here's what changed and what it resolves.

## What the skill looks like now

```text
skills/liatrio-brand-guidelines/
├── SKILL.md
├── agents/openai.yaml
├── assets/          (fonts, colors_and_type.css, 10 logo SVGs, 5 motifs, 21 previews)
└── references/      (design-system, component-recipes, asset-index, brand-site)
```

No `scripts/`, no `examples/`. The skill is now guidance and assets only.

**Logos.** All 7 PNGs are gone, replaced by 10 SVGs — the 8 canonical ones from `liatrio.ai/brand-logos/` plus the two stacked lockups, which exist only in the design-system bundle and aren't published on the site. That's 44 KB against the previous 243 KB, with four variants you didn't have before, including `logomark_Liatrio_background.svg` — the square mark that's the actual answer to "don't put the logomark on green," which the skill had been prohibiting without offering a fix. The three byte-identical reverse PNGs and their invented use cases are gone.

**Motifs.** `circuit-divider.svg` had no source in either canonical surface, so I removed it along with the two previews that were authored rather than copied (`brand-circuit-divider.html`, `brand-textures.html`). The [review](04ba908e-8a04-4533-ad6c-8c98cb773499) came back with four blocking findings. I independently verified all four, and all four are real — three of them are errors I introduced.

## Confirmed blocking

**The accessibility claim is numerically false.** I wrote "Primary Green on white passes large-text only" in `liatrio-design-system.md:122`. I computed the actual ratio: `#24AE1D` on white is **2.94:1**, which fails the 3:1 large-text floor stated three lines above it. Primary Green fails AA as text on white at any size. I copied this line from the bundle README without checking the math, and it's the worst kind of error to leave in a skill whose job includes running contrast audits — it would certify a failing combination as passing.

**My button-radius resolution was wrong.** I claimed "the design system's own button preview ships `border-radius: 6px`." It does not. The base `.btn` rule has no radius at all, the card label reads `Primary · solid · square`, and the file's header comment says "Real liatrio.ai buttons are SQUARE, uppercase, tracked." The single 6px rule in that file is on `.btn-nav`, explicitly labeled a soft-corner exception. My earlier grep matched only class-suffixed selectors and I read the nav exception as the general rule.

So there are actually three answers, not two: the bundle README says capsule 999px, the bundle preview says square, and liatrio.ai today says 6px (that part I re-confirmed — `--radius: 0.5rem` with buttons at `rounded-md`). 6px is still defensible as the most current evidence, but it's a decision that overrides both bundle sources, not the consensus I described. And the practical damage is real: the skill ships `components-buttons.html` as "recipe evidence" while its recipe file prescribes something different, so an agent gets two answers depending on which file it opens.

**`SKILL.md` contradicts its own button recipe on casing.** I listed "Sentence case everywhere, ALL CAPS only for eyebrow labels at 14px or smaller" as one of six invariants, and `liatrio-design-system.md:101` says sentence case for buttons specifically. But the recipe I edited ships `text-transform: uppercase` on a 14px primary button. Same underlying conflict as the radius — bundle prose says sentence-case buttons, the liatrio.ai capture says uppercase — and I asserted both sides in different files instead of resolving it.

**The PNG fallback claim 404s.** I wrote that PNG renders exist "at the same paths on liatrio.ai" beneath a table that includes the stacked lockups. Verified: `logo_Liatrio.png` and `logomark_Liatrio.png` return 200, but both stacked PNGs return 404 — which my own provenance note two sections earlier already implies, since the stacked variants aren't published on the site.

## Confirmed should-fix

The DM Sans sentence in `liatrio-brand-site.md:122` is garbled backwards — "Flag this only when auditing liatrio.ai's own code, where DM Sans is expected rather than a defect" says to flag it in the one place it's expected, inverting what `SKILL.md:88` correctly says.

The foreground row says "Five foreground levels" and lists four; the bundle's fifth is `border`, which I moved to its own table row.

Inputs get 4px in the radii list and 8px in the forms recipe. The bundle disagrees with itself here too (its forms preview contains both values), and I reproduced the disagreement without noticing.

The reviewer also flagged that `SKILL.md` spends three separate sections — Quick Start Workflow, Verification Loop, Workflow Checklist — restating the same steps, which is about a third of the router and three places for one rule to drift.

## One real gap neither of us caught earlier

The brand site has a **Social** tab publishing four official banners at `/social-graphics/Banner 1-4.png`. I verified all four return 200 and appear in the page chunk. They're absent from `brand-data.json` and absent from the skill — yet `social/hero image` is a first-class task mode in `SKILL.md`. An agent in that mode currently has no way to know official banners exist and will invent one.

## What the review confirmed as correct

Asset integrity came back clean: all 10 logo SVGs byte-identical to their claimed sources, no duplicates remaining, filenames matching the JSON inventory. The 120-icon list matches the live chunk exactly including ordering. Every hex in the staged files matches `brand-data.json`, and no palette or CMYK data got duplicated locally. All 38 files in the asset index exist, all 26 preview asset paths resolve, and the deletions broke nothing outside `docs/specs/`.

## Two of these need your call

The contrast fix, the DM Sans inversion, the PNG scope, the foreground count, and the input radius are unambiguous — I can just fix them. The button radius and button casing are genuine three-way source conflicts where I need to know which way you want the skill to land.

content.text:
![Liatrio button evidence](/tmp/lds/button-evidence.png)

## The evidence I'd missed

The bundle ships `uploads/web-capture-2026-04-28T19-14-08.json` — nine real DOM captures from liatrio.ai with full computed styles. I'd excluded `uploads/` from consideration early on as scratch material, which was a mistake: it's the primary source that settles both questions. Neither I nor the reviewer had opened it.

Here's what liatrio.ai actually ships:

| Element | Radius | Casing | Size / weight |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `LET'S TALK` filled CTA | none | uppercase, 0.05em | 14px / 600, padding 16×32 |
| `READ MORE` filled secondary | none | uppercase, 0.05em | 12px / 600, padding 12×20 |
| `Explore` outline button | none | sentence case | 14px / 500, padding 10×24 |
| `BLOG` category chip | none | uppercase, 0.05em | 11px / 700, padding 4×10 |
| `Let's Talk` nav button | **6px** | sentence case | 14px / 500, padding 8×16 |

The capture format only emits `border-radius` when it's non-zero, and it appears on exactly one of the nine elements. The primary CTA's own markup confirms it — `class="inline-block bg-[#89df00] text-background px-8 py-4 font-semibold text-sm uppercase tracking-wider"`, with no `rounded-*` class at all.

## What this means

**There are two button languages, not one.** Marketing CTAs are square and uppercase. Nav and in-app chrome uses the shadcn primitive at 6px, sentence case. My error was sampling the shadcn Button on the `/brand` documentation page — which is chrome, the same family as the nav button — and generalizing it to every button. The bundle's preview card was right all along, and its header comment ("Real liatrio.ai buttons are SQUARE, uppercase, tracked. Sourced from web captures of liatrio.ai") points at exactly this file.

Worth flagging: the reviewer caught that my claim was false, but its suggested resolution — keep 6px and present it as a decision overriding the bundle — is also wrong. Square is correct for brand CTAs.

**The casing rule needs rewording, not a carve-out.** Every uppercase element on the site is 11–14px and tracked, which already satisfies the bundle README's intent ("ALL-CAPS only for very small labels ≤14px"). What's wrong is my compression of that into "ALL CAPS only for eyebrow labels," which narrowed it to one component type. The accurate rule distinguishes by tracking: eyebrows at 0.14em, CTA labels and chips at 0.05em, everything else sentence case.

## Also: I was wrong to delete the circuit divider

The second capture file, `web-capture-2026-04-29T14-05-35.json`, contains a real liatrio.ai section-divider component — same `viewBox="0 0 1200 70"`, same `cd-glow` filter, same path data, same `hsl(84, 85%, 58%)` stroke. The `circuit-divider.svg` I deleted as "invented" is a faithful extraction of it, and the preview's subtitle even says "lifted from liatrio.ai." I've restored both files. `brand-textures.html` stays deleted — that one really is an authored CSS approximation, and the layering rule it illustrates is already written in the recipes.

## Recommendation

Buttons: square for brand CTAs (filled primary, filled secondary, outline) and chips; 6px for nav and in-app chrome; 999px stays reserved for pills, badges, and eyebrow capsules. Mark the bundle README's "CTA capsule" line as contradicted by the captures rather than silently dropping it.

Casing: sentence case for headlines, body, nav, and outline buttons. Uppercase only at 14px or smaller, tracked — 0.14em for eyebrows, 0.05em for filled CTA labels and chips.

The visual design looks solid with that subtle 6px border radius on the navigation button creating a nice visual distinction. I've found the key evidence that answers both questions — there's a bundle containing actual DOM captures from liatrio.ai with computed styles that provides the definitive source material.

Now I'm laying out the concrete findings: the radius rules broken down by component type (square for primary CTAs and chips, 6px for navigation and chrome, 999px for pills), the casing standards for high-signal buttons and category chips, and clarifying that the circuit-divider issue has already been corrected. I should also note that the reviewer's recommendation was off base too, so the user knows to verify these findings independently rather than just accepting the review at face value.

I'll present the evidence and the revised SKILL.md invariant that reconciles the bundle README's intent with what's actually shipped, then ask for confirmation before applying all the fixes.

You were right to push on this. Two shipped surfaces contradict the guidance, and I've now documented both rather than leaving a rule that reality violates.

## What I found

**liatrio.ai/enablement uses Primary Green as text on white.** Two uppercase section eyebrows — "What We Bring" and "How It Works" — render in `#24AE1D`. I didn't trust the "nearest background class" heuristic for this, so I walked the DOM ancestry with a parser: both are direct children of `<section class="bg-white">` with no intervening background. That's 2.94:1. At `text-base md:text-lg` semibold (16–18px) it doesn't clear the WCAG large-text bar either, since that needs 18.66px bold, so it fails both thresholds rather than just the normal-text one.

Worth noting how narrow this is. The site CSS emits exactly one `text-[#24ae1d]` utility, and Tailwind only generates arbitrary-value classes that are actually used. I checked eight pages — homepage, contact, about, services, blog, resources, platform, enablement — and `/enablement` is the only one. Everywhere else the site uses Bright Green `#89DF00` on dark, which is 9.98:1.

**The skill's own `brand-logo.html` preview does it too.** The `PREFERRED` badge sets `#24AE1D` on `rgba(36,174,29,0.14)` over white. Composited that's `#E0F4DF`, giving 2.54:1 at 10px — worse than the site's. This line is byte-identical to the bundle, so it came from the designer, not from us.

## How I resolved it

The contrast math doesn't bend, so I kept the rule and named the exceptions instead — which is what `SKILL.md` already demands of itself for source conflicts. The design system reference now has a "Two shipped surfaces break the light-surface rule" subsection recording both, classifying them as defects rather than precedent, and giving the compliant substitute: Grey 800 text with green carried by a fill or rule beside the label. The asset index warns against copying the badge treatment, alongside the existing off-palette preview caveats.

I also added the other half of the picture, which the original line was missing: **the restriction is specific to light surfaces.** Primary Green is fine as text on the dark palette — 5.65:1 on the canvas, 5.39:1 on cards, 6.43:1 on Grey 800. My earlier wording could have been read as a blanket ban, which would have been wrong in the opposite direction on a dark-first brand. Bright Green is now stated too, since it's the sharper case: 1.66:1 on white, 9.98:1 on the canvas.

## One thing I noticed but didn't act on

Those `/enablement` eyebrows are 16–18px uppercase tracked at `0.25em`, which exceeds the "uppercase only at 14px or smaller" rule we just settled on, and uses tracking that matches neither the 0.14em eyebrow token nor the 0.05em CTA value. It's the same page and the same two elements, so it may just be one off-spec section. I left the casing rule alone rather than widening it on a single data point, but say the word if you want me to dig into whether that treatment appears elsewhere.
